newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas slips in West, firms in East.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas slips in West, firms in East.

text.p: Additional natural gas supply available in Alberta pressured western Canadian prices Friday, but a rally in futures propped up prices in the East, traders said.
Spot gas at the AECO storage hub in Alberta was quoted at C$1.54/1.55 per gigajoule, down two cents from Thursday.
"We're starting to see receipt gas coming back, and the outage is supposed to end next week," a Calgary-based trader said.
July and July/October AECO were both talked at C$1.51-1.53 per MWh.
Westcoast Energy's 750 million cubic feet a day Fort Nelson gas plant in northeastern B.C., is expected to return to service next Wednesday following its maintenance outage.
Spot prices at Sumas, Wash., eased by about one cent to about $1.40 per million British thermal units (mmBtu), traders said.
In eastern Canada, prices at Niagara rose two cents to a high of $2.34 per mmBtu. Most deals were reported done in the low-$2.30s.
Fueling the uptick, market sources said, were the rising July Henry Hub futures to a high of $2.175, up 9.5 cents from Thursday.

Separately, Canadian Gas Association reported earlier today that total Canadian gas stocks rose 12.6 percent to 136.14 bcf last week, or 27.7 percent full. This compares with 29.6 percent full a year ago.
In the West, stocks were at 94.36 bcf, or 33.2 percent full, versus 41.2 percent a year ago. Eastern stocks rose ahead of year-ago tallies to 41.77 bcf, or 18 percent full.
